To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the local connectome fingerprint is highly correlated across individuals, and that this correlation can be used to predict a range of social and cognitive phenotypes.
the local architecture (i.e., the local connectome) of white matter fascicle bundles in the brain is a reliable marker that is predictive of a range of subject attributes.
the local connectome fingerprint is a reliable, complex, low-dimensional, and highly predictive measure of social, health and cognitive phenotypes in the human connectome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what the local connectome can tell us about the brain.
the local architecture of the brain’s white matter pathways.
understanding the relationship between brain structure and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a new way to measure brain structure that has both the sensitivity to detect meaningful differences between individuals and the specificity to detect meaningful differences among individuals.

the local connectome reflects meaningful aspects of the variability shared across subjects along several dimensions, which is a necessary step towards understanding the biological mechanisms that give rise to the human connectome.
the local connectome phenotype maps derived from diffusion MRI data are a reliable phenotypic marker of social, health and cognitive attributes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the local connectome fingerprint is a reliable and informative marker of the variability in the human connectome that is shared between subjects and is predictive of a range of social and biological phenotypes.
the architecture of white matter pathways in the brain reflects the predisposition and experiences that shape the social, cognitive, and health attributes of the individual.
the local connectome reflects a meaningful portion, but not all, of the variability shared among subjects along several dimensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local connectome can be a sensitive and specific marker for a range of attributes, including those related to social, health, or cognitive factors.
the local architecture and connectivity of white matter pathways is a meaningful and reliable marker of subject-specific phenotypic variation.
the local connectome can provide a new, quantitative way to characterize the human connectome, with the potential to provide insights into the relationship between connectomic structure and function.
